links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM responses under repeated prompting (five runs per question)
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest response stability (85.7%); GPT-4o showed lower reproducibility (62.9%). Differences were statistically significant (P < 0.05).
links.quote: GPT-4o outperformed the others in readability (FRE: 53.19) and linguistic fluency but showed lower reproducibility (62.9%).

links.outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (FRE, FKGL)
links.effect: GPT-4o had the best readability (FRE 53.19) among the three models. Differences were statistically significant. Grade-level results for the other models are not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: GPT-4o outperformed the others in readability (FRE: 53.19) and linguistic fluency but showed lower reproducibility (62.9%).

screen.reason: The study is an offline empirical comparison of three LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4) answering patient-centered questions about post-cardiac surgery rehabilitation, evaluated by clinical experts and readability metrics without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
